title: Drosophila proboscis extension response and GCaMP imaging for assaying food appeal based on grittiness
protocol: Prepare a 50 mM sucrose solution by adding 950 μL water to 50 μL of a 500 mM sucrose stock solution.
Weigh silica microsphere powder (∼2–4 mg).
Transfer the weighed silica microsphere powder to a 0.6 mL microfuge tube.
Add 50 mM sucrose solution (20–40 μL) to make a 10% w/v particle solution.
Mix the particle solution by pipetting with a 10 μL pipette tip for 5 seconds.
Seal the tube with parafilm and store at room temperature.
Use the prepared particle food within 3 days of preparation.
Attach a 1 mL pipette tip to soft rubber tubing with the narrow side pointing out.
Trim the narrow side of the 1 mL tip slightly with a razor blade.
Attach another 1 mL pipette to the wide end of the trimmed tip.
Aspirate a fly into the 1 mL pipette tip.
Attach a 200 μL tip to the end containing the fly.
Expel the fly into the 200 μL pipette tip.
Gently shake the pipette tip downward while blowing out air to trap the fly at the end of the tip with its head towards the open end.
Make a horizontal cut above the fly's head using a razor blade.
Draw the fly back slightly from the end of the 200 μL pipette by gentle inhalation.
Introduce a second cut at an angle above the fly's head.
Expel air to push the fly head out over the open end of the tip so that only the labellum is exposed.
Remove the 200 μL tip from the apparatus.
Insert a very small cotton ball with a sharp wooden stick under the fly to immobilize it.
Place each individual fly preparation on a wet paper towel to keep the fly hydrated if not used immediately.
If the flies are properly fixed, they will survive overnight in a humidified chamber containing wet paper.
Alternatives: The sharp wooden stick can be replaced with a 10 μL pipette tip overlaid with the top half of a second 10 μL pipette tip.
Saturate the fly with water before performing a PER assay with sugar/particle food.
Offer each fly a drop of water at the end of a 10 μL pipette tip to test if it is saturated.
Mix the particle food in a 200 μL microfuge tube by pipetting for 3 seconds.
Withdraw 2 μL of the particle food into a 10 μL pipette tip.
Pipette the particle food in and out of the tip 2 to 3 times to mix the contents thoroughly.
Make contact between the labellum and the drop at the end of the pipette tip for approximately 0.2 to 0.6 seconds.
Withdraw the liquid drop quickly from the fly to allow full extension of the proboscis.
Perform PER assays using 50 mM sucrose alone with a parallel group of flies as a control.
Test all the flies with 500 mM sucrose alone.
Discard flies that do not respond to the test.
The fly fully extends its proboscis and consumes food for ≥1 s.
The fly extends its proboscis and consumes food for <1 s.
The fly fails to extend its proboscis.
Include ≥ 12 flies in each trial (n=1).
Repeat the experiments 5 times on different days.
Cross tmc-Gal4 flies with the UAS-GCaMP6f,UAS-tdTomato line or alternatives.
Collect 20–30 F1 flies (UAS-GCaMP6f,UAS-tdTomato/+;tmc-Gal4/+).
Transfer 3–5 day-old flies to a fresh vial 1 day before dissecting the heads.
Obtain the chambers previously prepared and silicone lubricant.
Place a drop of silicone lubricant in the middle of the chamber.
Briefly anesthetize the flies by injecting CO2 into the vial or by incubating the vial on ice for 2–3 min.
Withdraw the fly by grabbing its wings with forceps and place it in a dissection well containing 1× PBS.
Dissect the head away from the body by cutting the neck with fine scissors.
Incubate the isolated head for 5–8 min in PBS until the proboscis fully extends and the labellum is in a closed state.
Transfer the fly head from dissection well to the chamber.
Immobilize the fly head in the silicone in the chamber.
Orient the head on one side with one eye facing up.
Pick the fly head with labellum in a closed state using forceps.
Hold the head carefully with one side facing up.
Attach one side of the labellum to the grease so that the labellum sticks to the grease.
If the proboscis is contracted, then hold the head and pull back slightly to fully extend the proboscis.
Attach the head on the grease so that one side of the labellum remains flat and unfolded.
Adjust the grease beneath the sample to make the labellum horizontal.
Add a drop of water (∼60 μL) to the chamber.
Remove any bubbles around the labellum.
Set up a laser scanning confocal microscope for imaging experiments.
Perform the imaging at room temperature (∼23°C).
Use a Zeiss LSM 700 upright confocal microscope with a w Plan-Apochromat 20× /1.0 water objective and 1.9× optical zoom.
Set the pinhole to 2.07 Airy Units = 4.1 μm section.
Scan at 614.4 ms per frame in line at 8 bits.
Acquire images at 256 × 256 pixels with ZEN SP5 software.
Use pixel sizes of 0.67 μm × 0.67 μm and image sizes of 171.8 μm × 171.8 μm.
Use the 488 nm laser excitation line to image EGFP.
Use the 555 nm laser excitation line to image tdTomato.
Acquire the bright-field image using the tdTomato channel.
Set the time series to record 3 images on the three channels at 614.4 ms intervals.
Place the slide with the plastic chamber containing the head on the microscope stage under the 20× water immersion objective.
Adjust focus to visualize S6.
Begin recording GCaMP6f, tdTomato fluorescence signals, and bright-field simultaneously.
Record ≥5 frames before introducing mechanical stimulus to establish baseline.
Apply mechanical force in one direction (5–40 μm) using a motorized micromanipulator controlled by Linlab 2 software.
Push the glass tip on the labellum in the proximal direction with the glass tip touching the cuticle.
Measure step distances using video recordings of bright-field images and Zeiss confocal or Fiji software.
Save videos in .lsm format.
Place the glass tip on the cuticle between L8 and S6 sensilla.
Re-adjust focus on the md-L neuron cell soma before applying mechanical stimuli.
Set XYZ parameters on Linlab 2 software (5–40 μm for one direction, 0 for others).
Load .lsm file into Fiji control panel by dragging it to the control panel.
Select Image>Color>Split channels in Fiji.
Combine the tdTomato and EGFP channel files into one video.
Select Image>Stacks>Tools>Combine in Fiji to merge channels.
Align the positions of the md-L neuron in the video using the template matching plugin.
Select the tdTomato signal in the soma of the md-L neuron as the region of interest (ROI).
Open Plugins>Template Matching>Align slices in stacks for alignment.
Obtain the fluorescence intensity in separate time series stacks for both the tdTomato and EGFP signals in the soma of the md-L neuron.
Use Plugins>Time series analyzer V3 to analyze the time series data.
Calculate the average EGFP fluorescence signal in the selected ROI using the time series analyzer plugin.
Select a rectangular region including the md neuron soma, and add it to the ROI manager.
Click “Get Average” to obtain the average signal intensity of the series of images in the stack.
Select bright field images at the base and at each peak stimulus.
Use Image>Lookup tables>Thermal to display the heatmap of GCaMP and tdTomato images.
Calculate changes in fluorescence using the formula: ΔR/R0 = (R − R0) / R0, where R0 = F0(GFP) / F0(tdTomato).
Normalize GCaMP fluorescence (F) to tdTomato fluorescence: R = F(GFP) / F(tdTomato).
Obtain base GCaMP and tdTomato fluorescence (F0) from the average of the 5 frames before stimulus application.
Calculate an average response curve ± SEM.
